$comment: Catalog of selectable aka-claude-tools additions. Drives the installer menu and documents the payload. 'recommended' additions are pre-selected at the install prompt.

additions.name: Secure base settings
additions.description: Deny-reads on credential paths (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, .env, keychains, …) plus conventional env/attribution defaults. Always safe to layer on. Nonessential-traffic opt-outs (telemetry/error-reporting/feedback) are NOT here. They live in the opt-in `telemetry-off` addition, so Remote Control works by default.

additions.name: leak-guard
additions.prompt: leak-guard: block secrets + internal identifiers in WEB queries [bun]?
additions.description: PreToolUse guard on WebSearch/WebFetch and the SearXNG MCP tools (WEB egress only, Bash egress is command-guard's surface). Blocks web queries/urls/prompts containing detected secrets (trufflehog), token/SSH-key shapes, and (if configured) your org's internal identifiers (CT_EGRESS_PATTERNS, read from the install-compiled org-egress.json sidecar, portable-subset regex only). Covers the SearXNG MCP surface so secure-deep-research's sensitive-topic path (routed through self-hosted SearXNG for privacy) is egress-scanned too (a no-op when no SearXNG server is configured). Runs under bun (like command-guard), a hard dependency: selecting leak-guard aborts the install if bun is absent, rather than shipping a default-on security guard silently disabled.

additions.name: command-guard
additions.prompt: command-guard, the sole Bash egress guard: credential exfil, curl|bash, startup-file writes, internal identifiers [bun]?
additions.description: PreToolUse guard on Bash, the SOLE Bash egress guard (leak-guard is web-only). Denies pipe-to-shell (curl | bash) and writes to shell startup files (~/.zshrc, ~/.bashrc, …, a persistence vector the secure-settings Edit/Write deny can't reach via a Bash redirection). On outbound commands (curl/wget/nc/…) it denies a detected secret (trufflehog), an org internal-identifier match (CT_EGRESS_PATTERNS via the shared sidecar), and a credential key-shape paired with the outbound tool. Alerts on nc/socat/sendmail/env-dump/inline-interpreter. Requires bun, a hard dependency: selecting command-guard aborts the install if bun is absent, rather than shipping a default-on security guard silently disabled.

additions.name: rtk-safe
additions.prompt: rtk-safe: conservative rtk rewrites for token savings [bun; needs rtk >= 0.49.0]?
additions.description: PreToolUse rewrite on Bash; requires bun and stable rtk >= 0.49.0. Rewrites supported standalone commands, including grep and rg, which keep their native flags, exit codes, and regex dialect. Leaves alone: head (rtk read --max-lines is not a head equivalent), anything carrying a shell operator or substitution, and any command with a standalone -h/--help (rtk's own parser would answer with its usage). Preserves project scripts, package-manager runners, and interpreter selection. Inert when rtk is absent, old, prerelease, or its version check fails. Installs read-only display-command approvals including rtk grep and rtk rg; find, git branch, and mutating/egress forms retain normal permission checks. The rtk rg approval REQUIRES command-guard, which blocks ripgrep's --pre/--hostname-bin/RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH exec vectors.

additions.name: Responsive status line
additions.description: Width-adaptive status line (git, context, usage). Resolves its own config dir, so it works in any isolated config folder. Runs under bun (a hard dependency of this addition, like command-guard), not a security boundary, so the bun requirement is acceptable.

additions.name: /wrap-up
additions.description: Repo-agnostic end-of-session handoff that PREPARES, never executes: summarize, verify (stop on failure), stage intentionally with a secret/artifact scan (or just propose the git add commands), draft a conventional commit message. Multi-user aware: leaves others' staged changes alone, stops over in-progress rebases, proposes a feature branch instead of working on main. Never commits, merges, or pushes unless explicitly asked.

additions.name: secure-deep-research
additions.prompt: secure-deep-research (privacy-aware research with per-claim adversarial verification)?
additions.description: Deep-research workflow with per-claim adversarial verification: search -> fetch -> 3-vote verify -> cited synthesis. Sensitive topics are conservatively classified, query-redacted, GATED for confirmation before any external query fires, fan-out-reduced, and routed through a self-hosted SearXNG MCP server (mcp__searxng__*). Normal topics use WebSearch/WebFetch at full fan-out. Model-tiered: Scope+Synthesize inherit the session model, Search/Fetch run on Haiku, Verify on Sonnet. Auto-registers as the /secure-deep-research skill. NOTE: the sensitive-topic path needs a self-hosted SearXNG MCP server. Without it, only the normal (WebSearch) path works.

additions.name: secure-research
additions.description: Everyday multi-source research workflow (the Claude Research shape): parallel researcher subagents gather cited findings, one bounded gap-check wave, then a grounded synthesis. No adversarial verify tournament, so cheaper than secure-deep-research. Reach for that when claims need per-claim verification. Same privacy handling: sensitive topics are conservatively classified, query-redacted, GATED before any external query, and routed through a self-hosted SearXNG MCP server (mcp__searxng__*). Normal topics use WebSearch/WebFetch. Model-tiered: Scope+Synthesize inherit the session model, researchers run on Haiku, gap-check on Sonnet. Auto-registers as the /secure-research skill. NOTE: the sensitive-topic path needs a self-hosted SearXNG MCP server. Without it, only the normal (WebSearch) path works.

additions.name: harness-pointer
additions.description: PreToolUse guard on Bash that intercepts org-configured commands and points the agent to the right approach for your environment (e.g. gh -> git). Guidance, not a security boundary. Ships OFF and empty. Most engineers want every CLI. Enable + configure via aka-claude-tools.config.

additions.name: shell-audit
additions.prompt: shell-audit (shell startup audit: aliases, secrets, persistence, git drift)?
additions.description: Read-only auditor + skill. Walks your shell rc and every file it sources (cycle-safe) and flags: hardcoded credentials (values redacted), persistence-suspicious patterns (pipe-to-shell, eval-of-fetched, DYLD/LD_PRELOAD, writes into other rc files), duplicate or dangling aliases, and git-baseline drift. A detective tripwire for the shell-startup slice. Nothing is modified. Not a substitute for launchd/cron/ssh review.

additions.name: telemetry-off
additions.prompt: telemetry-off: set DISABLE_TELEMETRY (turns OFF Remote Control)?
additions.description: Opt-in: sets DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 to opt out of Anthropic operational telemetry. Ships OFF because it disables Claude Code's Remote Control (driving the CLI from a claude.ai session). The default leaves it unset so Remote Control works.

additions.name: error-reporting-off
additions.description: Opt-in: sets DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING=1 to opt out of Sentry error reporting.

additions.name: feedback-off
additions.description: Opt-in: sets DISABLE_FEEDBACK_COMMAND=1 to disable the /feedback command, which sends conversation history to Anthropic on demand.

additions.name: autoupdater-off
additions.prompt: autoupdater-off: set DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER (manual `claude update` still works)?
additions.description: Opt-in: sets DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 to stop automatic background updates; `claude update` still works.

additions.name: feedback-survey-off
additions.description: Opt-in: sets CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FEEDBACK_SURVEY=1 to disable the 'How is Claude doing?' session quality surveys (telemetry-off already suppresses these).
